aiTerms.definition: Large Language Model. A neural network trained on vast text data capable of generating and understanding human language. Used in Wall-V chat and voice agents.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. A technique that combines LLM generation with retrieval from external knowledge bases to produce more accurate, grounded responses.
Natural Language Processing. A branch of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
The process of further training a pre-trained model on domain-specific data to improve performance for particular tasks.
Numerical vector representations of text that capture semantic meaning, used for similarity search and clustering in AI applications.
Vector Database. A database optimized for storing and querying high-dimensional vectors, used in RAG pipelines for semantic search.
The practice of designing and refining input prompts to elicit desired outputs from AI models.

businessTerms.definition: Customer Relationship Management. Software for managing interactions with current and potential customers, tracking leads, and sales pipelines.
Enterprise Resource Planning. Integrated management software that handles core business processes including finance, HR, manufacturing, and supply chain.
Software as a Service. A cloud-based software delivery model where applications are hosted and provided over the internet on a subscription basis.
Business to Business. Commercial transactions and relationships between two businesses rather than between a business and individual consumers.
Business to Consumer. Commercial transactions directly between a business and individual end consumers.
Minimum Viable Product. A product with just enough features to satisfy early users and gather feedback for future development.
Return on Investment. A performance metric measuring the gain or loss generated relative to the investment cost.
Key Performance Indicator. A measurable value that demonstrates how effectively a business is achieving key objectives.

technicalTerms.definition: Application Programming Interface. A set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate with each other.
Representational State Transfer. An architectural style for designing networked applications, using standard HTTP methods for communication.
A query language and runtime for APIs that allows clients to request exactly the data they need in a single request.
A user-defined HTTP callback triggered by an event in a source application, sending data to a specified URL in real time.
Software that acts as a bridge between an operating system or database and applications, especially on a network. In Next.js, functions that run before a request is completed.
Server-Side Rendering. A technique where pages are rendered on the server and sent as fully formed HTML to the client browser.
Client-Side Rendering. A technique where pages are rendered in the browser using JavaScript after the initial HTML is loaded.
Single Page Application. A web application that loads a single HTML page and dynamically updates content without full page reloads.

hostingTerms.definition: Virtual Private Server. A virtualized server environment that provides dedicated resources within a shared physical server.
Content Delivery Network. A distributed network of servers that delivers cached content to users based on geographic proximity.
Secure Sockets Layer. A cryptographic protocol that encrypts data transmitted between a web server and browser, indicated by HTTPS.
Domain Name System. The hierarchical naming system that translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
A web-based hosting control panel providing graphical interface and automation tools for managing web hosting accounts.
Web Host Manager. A server administration tool used by hosting providers to manage accounts, packages, and server settings.
The amount of time a server or system is operational and available, typically expressed as a percentage. Wall-V guarantees 99.9% uptime.
The maximum rate of data transfer across a network path, measured in bits per second or bytes per second.

paymentTerms.definition: Instant Payment Notification. A message sent by a payment processor to notify a merchant of a transaction event such as payment received or refunded.
Hash-based Message Authentication Code. A cryptographic technique used to verify the integrity and authenticity of a message, commonly used for webhook signature verification.
A pre-generated URL that directs a customer to a payment page for a specific product or service with amount and details pre-filled.
The process where a customer completes a purchase by providing payment and billing information.
A document issued by a seller to a buyer detailing the products, services, quantities, agreed prices, and payment terms.
A formal estimate of the cost for specific products or services, typically valid for a defined period.
A significant checkpoint in a project that marks the completion of a deliverable, often tied to a partial payment.

projectTerms.definition: The initial phase of a project focused on understanding requirements, goals, constraints, and stakeholder expectations.
A defined point in a project timeline marking the completion of a major deliverable or phase.
A fixed time period (typically 1-4 weeks) during which a specific set of work items must be completed in agile development.
An ordered list of features, tasks, and fixes to be addressed in a project, maintained and prioritized by the product owner.
A brief daily meeting where team members share what they accomplished, what they are working on, and any blockers they face.
A meeting held at the end of a sprint or project phase to reflect on what went well, what did not, and what to improve.

legalTerms.definition: General Data Protection Regulation. European Union regulation governing data protection and privacy for individuals within the EU and EEA.
California Consumer Privacy Act. A California state statute that enhances privacy rights and consumer protection for residents of California.
Data Processing Agreement. A legally binding contract between a data controller and a data processor specifying obligations for handling personal data.
Terms and Conditions. The legal agreement between a service provider and a user governing the use of a service or website.
Service Level Agreement. A commitment between a provider and client defining the level of service expected, including uptime, response time, and resolution time.
Non-Disclosure Agreement. A legal contract establishing a confidential relationship between parties to protect proprietary information.
Digital Millennium Copyright Act. United States copyright law that implements international treaties to protect digital content from unauthorized use.

marketingTerms.definition: Search Engine Optimization. The practice of optimizing website content and structure to improve visibility and ranking in organic search engine results.
Search Engine Marketing. A digital marketing strategy that increases website visibility in search engine results pages through paid advertising.
Pay Per Click. An advertising model where advertisers pay a fee each time their ad is clicked, commonly used in search and display advertising.
Click-Through Rate. The percentage of people who click on a link or advertisement out of the total who view it.
Cost Per Action. An advertising pricing model where advertisers pay only when a specific action (signup, purchase, download) is completed.
Customer Acquisition Cost. The total cost of acquiring a new customer, including marketing and sales expenses divided by the number of new customers.
Lifetime Value. The total revenue a business can expect to generate from a single customer throughout their entire relationship.
The rate at which customers stop doing business with a company, expressed as a percentage of total customers over a given period.
